# LAVS — Local Agent View Service

> LAVS lets a local AI agent expose structured data as interactive UI views in the user's browser, and drive those views in one direction: agent → view. A LAVS "bundle" is a `lavs.json` manifest (endpoints + view) + handler scripts + an optional HTML view. Agents call endpoints via a CLI (`lavs call`) or MCP tools (`lavs_<endpoint>`); views auto-refresh via SSE, and pure UI commands (`notify` endpoints, SPEC §12) reach the view layer without touching data.

Site: https://jeffkit.github.io/lavs/
Repo: https://github.com/jeffkit/lavs
License: MIT

## Quick start (from zero)

- 5-minute walkthrough with a runnable demo bundle: https://jeffkit.github.io/lavs/guide/quick-start
- Source-run alternative: clone https://github.com/jeffkit/lavs then `pnpm install && pnpm build`; demo lives at `examples/quickstart/demo`.

## Install

- npm: `lavs-runtime` (CLI + host + MCP server), `lavs-types`, `lavs-client` (HTTP client), `lavs-view` (view-side SDK, ships a prebuilt IIFE for no-build views).
- Requires Node.js >= 20.

## Core workflow (agent side)

1. `lavs discover --registry-dir <dir>` — list available bundles/endpoints.
2. `lavs view --registry-dir <dir>` — start local HTTP host + open the browser view (SSE live).
3. `lavs call <endpoint> --agent-dir <bundle-dir> --input '<json>'` — query or mutate; mutations auto-refresh the view. stdout is clean JSON.
4. Optional: `lavs serve --agent-dir <dir>` (single bundle) or `lavs serve-registry` (multi-bundle) expose endpoints as MCP tools `lavs_<endpoint>` for MCP hosts.

## Endpoint methods

- `query` — read data. No view notification.
- `mutation` — write data. Broadcasts `tool_executed` agent-action; view refreshes.
- `notify` — pure UI command, no data side effects, `handler` optional. Broadcasts `ui_command` agent-action with `command` + `args`; the view handles known commands locally and MUST fall back to refresh for unknown ones.
- `subscription` — SSE stream from the view side; not exposed as agent tools.

## Authoring a bundle

- A bundle = `lavs.json` (declare `contentType`, `endpoints`, `view.component`) + handler scripts (plain Node scripts: stdin/args in, JSON to stdout) + optional `view/index.html`.
- The `view.component` field in the manifest is REQUIRED to get a rendered view (e.g. `{"type":"local","path":"./view/index.html"}`); a view dir alone is not picked up.
- Handlers: `script` (TS + Python runtimes), `function`/`http`/`mcp` (TS runtime only).
- Data written by handlers lives under the bundle's own `data/` directory.
- Guide: https://jeffkit.github.io/lavs/guide/create-bundle
- Manifest reference: https://jeffkit.github.io/lavs/reference/manifest

## View-side SDK (@lavs/view)

```html
<script src="lavs-view.iife.js"></script>
<script>
  const view = LAVSView.connect({
    refresh: loadItems,            // data changed (or unknown command) → reload
    commands: { setTheme(args) { /* ... */ } },  // UI command registry
  });
  const items = await view.call('getItems');     // call an endpoint
</script>
```

- One-way control invariant: views can call endpoints and react to agent-actions; there is no channel for a view to address the agent.
- Guide: https://jeffkit.github.io/lavs/guide/ui-commands

## CLI reference

- All commands (`discover` / `call` / `view` / `host` / `daemon` / `init` / `validate` / `serve` / `serve-registry`): https://jeffkit.github.io/lavs/guide/cli
- CLI vs MCP decision guide: https://jeffkit.github.io/lavs/guide/cli-vs-mcp

## Protocol spec

- Overview: https://jeffkit.github.io/lavs/spec/overview
- View Dispatch Protocol v1.1 (content-type as primary abstraction): https://jeffkit.github.io/lavs/spec/v1.1-dispatch
- UI Command Protocol §12 (v1.2-draft, normative source): https://github.com/jeffkit/lavs/blob/main/docs/SPEC.md
- JSON Schema for lavs.json: https://github.com/jeffkit/lavs/blob/main/schema/lavs-manifest.schema.json

## Official bundles (in repo, `bundles/`)

- `todo-list` — CRUD + priority/tags + `setFilter`/`setCompact` UI commands (reference bundle)
- `daily-note` — time-series notes, date grouping, full-text search
- `data-table` — generic sortable/filterable table, CSV export
- `bookmark` — URL manager with tags and card layout

## Security notes

- ENFORCED: path-traversal checks on script handlers, input JSON-Schema validation, execution timeouts.
- ADVISORY only (not OS-enforced): `fileAccess`, `networkAccess`, `maxMemory`. Sandbox untrusted bundles with Docker/nsjail.
- Views must treat `ui_command` args as untrusted input.

- Implementation status and honest caveats: https://jeffkit.github.io/lavs/reference/status
